COLLEGE ATHLETE NAME, IMAGE, AND LIKENESS (NIL) COMPENSATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan T. Ellis · Women's basketball

WHAT THIS DOCUMENT COVERS: THE STATUTORY NIL REGIME AGAINST SCHOOLS AND ATHLETIC ASSOCIATIONS, NOT A PRIVATE CONSENT-TO-USE RELEASE
California Education Code section 67456 is part of the Student Athlete Bill of Rights (Education Code Part 40.3) and provides that a postsecondary educational institution shall not uphold any rule, requirement, standard, or other limitation that prevents a student participating in intercollegiate athletics at that institution from earning compensation as a result of the use of the student's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation, and that the same student's scholarship eligibility is not affected by earning that compensation. This statute regulates a different relationship than this corpus's separate Model/Publicity Release information sheet, which addresses the right-of-publicity consent a person gives a private party (such as an advertiser) to use that person's own identity under Civil Code section 3344. Section 67456 instead addresses whether a student athlete's own postsecondary institution, or an athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics, may itself restrict that student's ability to earn compensation from third parties for use of the student's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation. Section 67456's text does not itself supply, or substitute for, whatever separate consent a student athlete may still need to give any specific third party under the general right-of-publicity framework before that third party could use the athlete's identity.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "shall not uphold any rule, requirement, standard, or other limitation that prevents a student of that institution participating in intercollegiate athletics from earning compensation as a result of the use of the student’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation"
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (a)(1), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "Earning compensation from the use of a student’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation shall not affect the student’s scholarship eligibility."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (a)(1), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of what California's own Student Athlete Bill of Rights framework restricts (institution and athletic-association conduct toward a student athlete) as distinct from what a general right-of-publicity consent statute like Civil Code section 3344 addresses (a private party's use of a person's identity with that person's consent) — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation, and not a claim that Section 67456 itself creates, defines, or limits the separate consent that a right-of-publicity statute would otherwise require for a specific third-party use. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law interpreting Section 67456 or the scope of a student athlete's NIL rights is cited anywhere in this document; every authority clause here rests on the statute's own text only. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific institutional rule, athletic-association policy, team contract, or NIL contract complies with, or is prohibited by, Section 67456 or any other law, and completing this information sheet does not itself resolve any of those questions or constitute legal advice about any reader's specific situation.

ATHLETIC ASSOCIATIONS AND CONFERENCES — INCLUDING THE NCAA BY NAME — ARE ALSO BARRED FROM PREVENTING NIL COMPENSATION, AND FROM PENALIZING THE INSTITUTION
Section 67456's prohibition on restricting a student athlete's NIL compensation is not limited to the student's own institution. The statute separately states that an athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics — naming the National Collegiate Athletic Association as one example, without limiting the prohibition to that organization — shall not prevent a student of a postsecondary educational institution from earning compensation as a result of the use of the student's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation. The statute goes further still: the same kind of athletic association, conference, or other group or organization also shall not prevent the postsecondary educational institution itself from participating in intercollegiate athletics as a result of a student athlete's NIL compensation — that is, the statute bars retaliation against the school, not only against the individual athlete.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics, including, but not limited to, the National Collegiate Athletic Association, shall not prevent a student of a postsecondary educational institution participating in intercollegiate athletics from earning compensation as a result of the use of the student’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (a)(2), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "An athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics, including, but not limited to, the National Collegiate Athletic Association, shall not prevent a postsecondary educational institution from participating in intercollegiate athletics as a result of the compensation of a student athlete for the use of the student’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (a)(3), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of what it says about athletic associations, conferences, and similar organizations generally — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation, and not a claim about how any specific athletic association's current bylaws, rules, or NIL policies compare to what this statute requires, which this document does not research. The statute's own phrase "including, but not limited to, the National Collegiate Athletic Association" means the prohibition is not confined to the NCAA by name; this document does not identify every organization the phrase might reach. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law applying this subdivision to any specific association's rule is cited here. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific institutional rule, athletic-association policy, team contract, or NIL contract complies with, or is prohibited by, Section 67456 or any other law.

A SEPARATE, OPPOSITE-DIRECTION RULE: INSTITUTIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS MAY NOT PAY A PROSPECTIVE STUDENT ATHLETE NIL-RELATED COMPENSATION
Section 67456 contains two rules that point in different directions and should not be collapsed into one another. Subdivision (a) bars a postsecondary institution or athletic association from stopping a current student athlete from earning outside NIL compensation from third parties. Subdivision (b) instead separately bars the postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics from itself providing compensation to a prospective student athlete in relation to that athlete's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation. Read together, the statute's own text protects a student athlete's ability to earn NIL compensation from others; it does not, by its own terms, permit the institution or association itself to pay a not-yet-enrolled prospective athlete in connection with NIL as a recruiting inducement.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics shall not provide a prospective student athlete with compensation in relation to the athlete’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (b), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of a textual distinction between what subdivision (a) permits (a student athlete earning outside compensation) and what subdivision (b) restricts (the institution or association itself paying a prospective athlete) — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation. The statute's list of restricted payors is "a postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics"; this document does not resolve, and the statute's text does not on its face address, whether a separate, non-institutional third-party organization (for example, an independent collective not itself an athletic association, conference, or other group with authority over intercollegiate athletics) falls inside or outside that list. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law construing subdivision (b) or the phrase "prospective student athlete" is cited here. This document is informational only and does not itself determine whether any specific payment to any specific prospective or current student athlete is permitted or prohibited under this section.

RIGHT TO OBTAIN LICENSED PROFESSIONAL REPRESENTATION FOR NIL CONTRACTS AND LEGAL MATTERS
Section 67456 states that a postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics shall not prevent a California student participating in intercollegiate athletics from obtaining professional representation in relation to contracts or legal matters, including representation provided by athlete agents or legal representation provided by attorneys. The statute's own text further specifies that this representation must come from persons licensed by the state: athlete-agent representation must be provided by persons licensed under Chapter 2.5 of Division 8 of the Business and Professions Code (commencing with Section 18895), and legal representation must be provided by attorneys licensed under Article 1 of Chapter 4 of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code (commencing with Section 6000). Section 67456 also states that athlete agents representing student athletes must comply with the federal Sports Agent Responsibility and Trust Act, codified starting at Section 7801 of Title 15 of the United States Code, in their relationships with student athletes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics shall not prevent a California student participating in intercollegiate athletics from obtaining professional representation in relation to contracts or legal matters, including, but not limited to, representation provided by athlete agents or legal representation provided by attorneys."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (c)(1), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "Professional representation obtained by student athletes shall be from persons licensed by the state. Professional representation provided by athlete agents shall be by persons licensed pursuant to Chapter 2.5 (commencing with Section 18895) of Division 8 of the Business and Professions Code. Legal representation of student athletes shall be by attorneys licensed pursuant to Article 1 (commencing with Section 6000) of Chapter 4 of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (c)(2), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "Athlete agents representing student athletes shall comply with the federal Sports Agent Responsibility and Trust Act, established in Chapter 104 (commencing with Section 7801) of Title 15 of the United States Code, in their relationships with student athletes."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (c)(3), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Section 67456's own text describing and cross-referencing the Business and Professions Code licensing chapters and the federal Sports Agent Responsibility and Trust Act; it does not independently fetch or quote the text of Business and Professions Code Section 18895 et seq., Section 6000 et seq., or 15 U.S.C. Section 7801 et seq. themselves, so this document does not verify what those separately cross-referenced provisions require beyond what Section 67456's own text states about them. Subdivision (c)(1)'s protected class is phrased as "a California student participating in intercollegiate athletics," which is not verbatim the same phrase ("a student of that institution participating in intercollegiate athletics") used in subdivision (a)(1) elsewhere in this same section; this document notes that textual difference without resolving whether it is meant to narrow or simply restate the same protected group. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law is cited here. This document is informational only and does not itself determine whether any specific person's representation of any specific student athlete satisfies this section's licensing requirements.

A COST-OF-ATTENDANCE SCHOLARSHIP IS NOT "COMPENSATION" UNDER THIS SECTION, AND CANNOT BE REVOKED FOR EARNING NIL MONEY OR GETTING LEGAL REPRESENTATION
Section 67456's own text draws a line between a student athlete's cost-of-attendance scholarship and the NIL compensation the section otherwise addresses. It states that a scholarship from the postsecondary educational institution in which a student is enrolled, providing the student with the cost of attendance at that institution, is not compensation for purposes of this section, and that a scholarship shall not be revoked as a result of a student earning compensation or obtaining legal representation pursuant to this section. This is consistent with, and reinforces, the separate statement elsewhere in the same section that earning NIL compensation does not affect a student's scholarship eligibility.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A scholarship from the postsecondary educational institution in which a student is enrolled that provides the student with the cost of attendance at that institution is not compensation for purposes of this section, and a scholarship shall not be revoked as a result of earning compensation or obtaining legal representation pursuant to this section."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (d), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This clause is limited to what Section 67456's own text says about a cost-of-attendance scholarship and this specific section's compensation and legal-representation provisions; the statute's text as quoted here does not address, and this document does not research, other financial-aid rules (for example, need-based aid recalculation under federal financial aid law), NCAA or conference scholarship rules apart from this statute, or the tax treatment of NIL income. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of how it treats a cost-of-attendance scholarship for purposes of this section — not a claim about which state's law, or which other body of financial-aid or tax law, governs any reader's situation. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law is cited here. This document is informational only and does not itself determine whether any specific scholarship was properly awarded, maintained, or revoked.

DISCLOSURE TO THE INSTITUTION, AND THE PROHIBITION ON AN NIL CONTRACT THAT CONFLICTS WITH A TEAM CONTRACT
Section 67456 imposes disclosure obligations tied to a student athlete's NIL contract. Its text states that a student athlete shall not enter into a contract providing compensation for use of the athlete's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation if a provision of that contract is in conflict with a provision of the athlete's team contract. Separately, the statute's text requires a student athlete who does enter into such a compensation contract to disclose the contract to an official of the institution, to be designated by the institution. The statute also imposes a corresponding disclosure obligation running the other direction: an institution asserting that a conflict of the kind just described exists must disclose to the athlete, or to the athlete's legal representation, the relevant contractual provisions that are in conflict.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A student athlete shall not enter into a contract providing compensation to the athlete for use of the athlete’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation if a provision of the contract is in conflict with a provision of the athlete’s team contract."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (e)(1), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "A student athlete who enters into a contract providing compensation to the athlete for use of the athlete’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation shall disclose the contract to an official of the institution, to be designated by the institution."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (e)(2), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  "An institution asserting a conflict described in paragraph (1) shall disclose to the athlete or the athlete’s legal representation the relevant contractual provisions that are in conflict."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (e)(3), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: Section 67456's own text, as quoted here, does not specify a deadline by which the athlete's disclosure to the institution must be made (for example, before or after signing), the form that disclosure must take, or any penalty for a student athlete's failure to disclose; this document does not supply those missing details or assume any particular disclosure procedure. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of what its own text requires — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation, and not a claim that any specific NIL contract does or does not conflict with any specific team contract, which depends on the actual wording of both documents. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law construing this disclosure or conflict provision is cited here. This document is informational only and does not itself resolve any conflict between an NIL contract and a team contract, or determine that any specific disclosure satisfies this section.

A TEAM CONTRACT CANNOT BAR COMMERCIAL NIL USE OUTSIDE OFFICIAL TEAM ACTIVITIES — AND THE STATUTE'S TEXT LIMITS THIS RULE TO CERTAIN CONTRACTS
Section 67456's text separately restricts what a postsecondary educational institution's athletic program can put in a team contract. It states that a team contract of a postsecondary educational institution's athletic program shall not prevent a student athlete from using the athlete's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation for a commercial purpose when the athlete is not engaged in official team activities. The same subdivision then states the Legislature's intent that this particular prohibition applies only to contracts entered into, modified, or renewed on or after the enactment of this section.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A team contract of a postsecondary educational institution’s athletic program shall not prevent a student athlete from using the athlete’s name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation for a commercial purpose when the athlete is not engaged in official team activities. It is the intent of the Legislature that this prohibition shall apply only to contracts entered into, modified, or renewed on or after the enactment of this section."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 67456 (California Legislative Information text, as amended by Stats. 2021, Ch. 159, Sec. 3 (SB 26), operative Sept. 1, 2021) — subd. (f), California Education Code, Student Athlete Bill of Rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=67456.)
  Known gap: This subdivision's own text limits its prohibition to contracts "entered into, modified, or renewed on or after the enactment of this section," but Section 67456 has been amended more than once since it was first added; this document, having fetched only the section's current, in-force text, does not independently trace which specific enactment or amendment date this legislative-intent statement refers to, and does not resolve that dating question for any specific team contract. The statute's text also does not define "official team activities"; this document does not supply that definition. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of what its own text and stated legislative intent say — not a claim about which state's law governs any reader's situation, and not a claim that any specific team-contract provision does or does not fall within this prohibition. This document's connection to CourtListener's case-search tool had already returned a daily-quota-exhausted (HTTP 429) response before any search could be run, so no case law construing this subdivision is cited here. This document is informational only and does not itself determine that any specific team contract complies with, or violates, this section.

NIL CONTRACT DISCLOSURE TO INSTITUTION — DECLARATION AND SIGNATURE
I, Jordan T. Ellis, a student athlete participating in intercollegiate Women's basketball at State University, state that I have entered into a contract providing compensation for use of my name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation with Jordan Morgan.

Description of compensation: $500 flat fee

I am disclosing this contract to State University's designated official as described in Education Code section 67456(e)(2). This disclosure does not itself determine whether any provision of this contract conflicts with any provision of my team contract with State University's athletic program.

Signature: _________________________
Date: September 1, 2026

[This information sheet and this disclosure are not, by themselves, legal advice, and do not themselves determine whether any specific rule, requirement, standard, team-contract provision, or NIL contract complies with, or is prohibited by, Education Code section 67456 or any other law.]

citations.quote: A postsecondary educational institution, athletic association, conference, or other group or organization with authority over intercollegiate athletics shall not prevent a California student participating in intercollegiate athletics from obtaining professional representation in relation to contracts or legal matters, including, but not limited to, representation provided by athlete agents or legal representation provided by attorneys.

expectedJSON.body: Section 67456's own text draws a line between a student athlete's cost-of-attendance scholarship and the NIL compensation the section otherwise addresses. It states that a scholarship from the postsecondary educational institution in which a student is enrolled, providing the student with the cost of attendance at that institution, is not compensation for purposes of this section, and that a scholarship shall not be revoked as a result of a student earning compensation or obtaining legal representation pursuant to this section. This is consistent with, and reinforces, the separate statement elsewhere in the same section that earning NIL compensation does not affect a student's scholarship eligibility.

expectedJSON.body: Section 67456 imposes disclosure obligations tied to a student athlete's NIL contract. Its text states that a student athlete shall not enter into a contract providing compensation for use of the athlete's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation if a provision of that contract is in conflict with a provision of the athlete's team contract. Separately, the statute's text requires a student athlete who does enter into such a compensation contract to disclose the contract to an official of the institution, to be designated by the institution. The statute also imposes a corresponding disclosure obligation running the other direction: an institution asserting that a conflict of the kind just described exists must disclose to the athlete, or to the athlete's legal representation, the relevant contractual provisions that are in conflict.

expectedJSON.body: Section 67456's text separately restricts what a postsecondary educational institution's athletic program can put in a team contract. It states that a team contract of a postsecondary educational institution's athletic program shall not prevent a student athlete from using the athlete's name, image, likeness, or athletic reputation for a commercial purpose when the athlete is not engaged in official team activities. The same subdivision then states the Legislature's intent that this particular prohibition applies only to contracts entered into, modified, or renewed on or after the enactment of this section.
